title: Workload-sliced latency-quality maps for batching and KV-cache policy comparisons
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Run a multidimensional evaluation that produces latency-vs-quality maps (per-workload slice) comparing a matrix of batching and KV-cache policies. The goal is to build interpretable maps that help reviewers and the rollout system decide which config changes (PRs) are safe for a given workload profile and SLO band. This ticket ties evaluation artifacts to the regression monitor so config changes can be gated automatically when quality regressions exceed configured tolerances for high-impact slices.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a set of latency-vs-quality maps (CSV + plotted PNGs) for the canonical workloads (short-chat, long-chat, summarization, embeddings-bulk) across the defined config grid
Define workload slicing rules and implement the slicer in eval-runner v2 so slices are reproducible and referenced by slice_id
Integrate map outputs with the regressions service: provide a digest (slice_id + metric deltas + confidence) that can be consumed by PR gating rules
Document safe rollback recommendations (config keys + thresholds) and add them to the rollout playbook
Automated nightly run that covers the reduced grid for smoke checks and posts to the performance dashboard
tasks: Design grid: choose batch sizes, microbatch thresholds, kvcache TTLs, eviction policy (LRU/ARC), prefix-cache TTL and chunking — owner: Liam — 1d
Implement workload slicer and canonical prompt sets (owner: Maya) — 2d
Add CSV/JSON output schema to eval-runner v2 to include slice_id and provenance (model, seed, hardware) — owner: Priya — 1d
Run full grid on dedicated staging fleet (owner: infra-runner) — 2d
Compute metrics and generate plotted maps + store artifacts (owner: analytics) — 1d
Hook digest generation into regressions service and add sample PR-gate policy (owner: reliability) — 1d
Write rollout guidance and add to Console rollout playbook (owner: product) — 1d
evaluation_plan: We will run a full factorial sweep across: batch_size in {1,4,8,16,32}, microbatch_threshold in {1,8,32}, kvcache_ttl_seconds in {0,30,300,3600}, eviction_policy in {LRU,ARC}. For each cell run N=50 prompts per slice using three seeds for sampling variability and compute per-slice mean and 95% bootstrap CIs for latency and quality metrics. Produce latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) and per-token latency distributions. Quality metrics are workload-specific (see 'metrics'). Map points will plot p95 latency on x-axis vs delta-quality on y-axis relative to baseline config (batch_size=1, kvcache_ttl=300, microbatch=1).
datasets: edge-case-prompts (300 prompts with malformed tokens and long-tail behaviors)
metrics: quality_delta_primary (workload-specific): QA-accuracy or ROUGE-L or embedding-cosine-mean
logprob_shift_mean (mean Δ of token logprobs compared to baseline)
generation_divergence_rate (fraction of responses with structural errors)
results_summary: Preliminary smoke runs on a small subset (batch_size {1,8,32}, kvcache_ttl {0,300}) show expected latency reductions moving to batch_size=32 for the embeddings workload (p95 latency ~ -40%) but a measurable embedding-cosine-mean regression of ~0.015 vs baseline (relative). For short-chat prompts, microbatching at higher thresholds (>=32) gives a small p95 gain but increases generation_divergence_rate in 3% of samples for the long-short-turn prompts. These are only preliminary and require the full grid to confirm statistical significance.
follow_up: If full grid confirms embedding quality regression > 0.02 for specific batch+ttl cells, add those cells to the PR-gate denylist and annotate with rollback recommendations
Add a lightweight agent in CI that runs the reduced-slice smoke-check (4 slices covering high-impact customers) on config-change PRs
Explore targeted microbatching heuristics based on input length and slice metadata instead of uniform thresholds
Schedule a joint review with Product and Reliability to agree on acceptable tradeoff bands for each workload slice
